title: AU Emerging Global Leader Scholarship (AU EGLS)
program_type: University merit scholarship awarded at admission, with a separate two-step scholarship application required
funding_type: Full coverage of all billable AU expenses (tuition, room, board), university-funded, plus AU EGL Partial Scholarships valued up to US$40,000 per year
administering_authority: American University, Office of Enrollment (Undergraduate Admissions)
implementing_agency: American University, Office of Enrollment — International Admissions
programme_action: AU Emerging Global Leader Scholarship (full award) and the AU EGL Partial Scholarships
description: The AU Emerging Global Leader Scholarship (AU EGLS) is a competitive scholarship at American University in Washington, DC for international first-year students who will need a non-immigrant visa (preferably F-1 or J-1) to study in the United States. The full award covers all billable AU expenses — full tuition, room, and board — for two international students and is renewable for a total of four years of undergraduate study based on continued satisfactory academic performance. AU also offers AU EGL Partial Scholarships valued at up to US$40,000 per year to additional applicants who complete the EGLS process successfully. The scholarship does not cover non-billable expenses such as mandatory health insurance, books, airline tickets, taxes, and miscellaneous expenses, which AU estimates at approximately US$4,000 per year.

award_types: AU Emerging Global Leader Scholarship (full coverage of all billable AU expenses)
AU EGL Partial Scholarship (up to US$40,000 per year)
programme_structure.award_types_detail: AU's dedicated AU EGLS application page states that the scholarship covers all billable AU expenses (full tuition, room, and board) for two international students, and that AU additionally offers AU EGL Partial Scholarships valued at up to US$40,000 per year. AU's First-Year Merit Awards page states that AU offers up to eight additional AU EGL Partial Scholarships valued at up to US$40,000 per year. No additional application process is required for the partial scholarships; candidates are drawn from applicants who complete the AU EGLS process successfully.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Renewable for a total of four years of undergraduate study based on continued satisfactory academic performance.
programme_structure.intake: Fall semester (August) entry; AU recommends AU EGLS applicants apply Regular Decision for Fall 2027. Spring applicants are not part of the EGLS cycle — AU instructs applicants to apply for the fall semester, not spring.

status_note: Open for the Fall 2027 entry cycle. AU's dedicated AU EGLS application page publishes 15 January 2027 for both application steps, with finalists and award winners notified by 1 April 2027. Because today is 2026-10-10, the deadline has not yet passed. Next expected cycle: Fall 2028 entry, which should open with the Common Application in August 2027.
verification_notes: Verified on 2026-10-10 by reading eight official american.edu pages: the AU EGLS application page, the First-Year Merit Awards page, the legacy Emerging Global Leader Scholarship page, the international first-year instructions checklist, the ISSS AY 2026-2027 undergraduate cost guide, the ISSS financial documents page, the ISSS Applying for a Visa page, and the Decision Plans and Deadlines FAQ. Award name, full-award benefit (all billable AU expenses — full tuition, room, board — for two international students needing a non-immigrant visa), the excluded non-billable expenses at approximately US$4,000 per year, the AU EGL Partial Scholarships valued up to US$40,000 per year with up to eight awards, four-year renewability, the two-step application with both steps due 15 January 2027, the US$4,000 bank letter and AU Declaration of Finances Form, the accepted English tests and their published minimum scores, the ineligibility rules, the preference criteria and the interview stage were all confirmed from official text. Unresolved internal conflicts on AU's own site are recorded as risk flags and in verification.programme_check_required: the EGLS deadline (15 January on the award page versus 1 December in the Decision Plans FAQ), the number of full awards (two on current pages versus one on the legacy page), the AU DFF first-year amount (US$87,374 versus US$83,680), and the count of partial scholarships (up to eight, published only on the merit page). AU's '85/4.5' TOEFL minimum is not defined by the source and was not interpreted.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: The Common Application for the following fall term opens 1 August. AU EGLS applicants submit both Step 1 and Step 2 by 15 January; AU strongly recommends applicants living outside the United States apply by 1 September, and recommends Regular Decision for the AU EGLS.
application_deadline.application_period: Fall 2027 entry: Step 1 (Common Application and all supporting documents) and Step 2 (AU EGLS application and essays via the applicant portal) both due before 15 January 2027. Late applications will not be considered. AU strongly recommends applicants outside the U.S. apply by 1 September.
application_deadline.official_rule: Step 1: Applicants must first submit their Common Application and all supporting documents before January 15, 2027. Step 2: Applicants must submit the AU EGLS application and essays via their applicant portal by the required January 15, 2027 deadline. Step 1 must be completed before Step 2. Late applications will not be considered.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: CONFLICT ON AU'S OWN SITE: the Decision Plans and Deadlines FAQ states that AU EGLS applicants must submit their Common Application prior to December 1 and submit the AU EGL Scholarship application via their Future Eagle Portal by December 1, to be considered for the scholarship. The dedicated AU EGLS application page states January 15, 2027. Treat 1 December 2026 as the safe working deadline and confirm with intadm@american.edu before relying on the later date.

programme_duration.renewal_note: The AU EGLS is renewable for a total of four years of undergraduate study, based on continued satisfactory academic performance. AU states there are no increases in scholarship amounts from year to year for its merit awards.

funding.scholarship_type: Full-coverage institutional scholarship (all billable AU expenses) plus partial awards
funding.monthly_amount_note: AU does not publish a monthly stipend or living allowance for the AU EGLS. The benefit is defined as coverage of all billable AU expenses.
funding.living_allowance: Room and board are covered because they are billable AU expenses. No separate living allowance or stipend is published.
funding.travel_amount_note: Airline tickets are explicitly listed by AU as a non-billable expense that the student must pay out of pocket. No travel allowance is published.
funding.fully_funded_note: AU's own wording is that the full AU EGLS 'covers all billable AU expenses (full tuition, room, and board)'. Mandatory health insurance, books, airline tickets, taxes, and miscellaneous expenses remain the student's responsibility at approximately US$4,000 per year, so the award is full-coverage of billable costs rather than an all-inclusive full ride. AU does not use the phrase 'fully funded' on the official award pages.

tuition.conditions: Covered as a billable AU expense. AU's ISSS undergraduate cost guide for academic year 2026-2027 lists tuition of US$62,680 at 12-17 credits per semester. AU states an increase of approximately 5-7% should be anticipated for each succeeding academic year.

travel_allowance.note: Not published in official source; airline tickets are explicitly excluded from the award

visa_support.note: Not published. AU's Applying for a Visa page lists the SEVIS fee, DS-160 completion and payment of the visa fee as student obligations, with no amounts published.

insurance.note: Mandatory health insurance is explicitly excluded from the award. AU's ISSS undergraduate cost guide for 2026-2027 lists health insurance at US$2,506.

book_allowance.note: Books are explicitly excluded from the award. AU's ISSS undergraduate cost guide for 2026-2027 lists books at US$1,200.

family_allowance.note: Not published. AU's ISSS cost guides advise married students to add at least US$5,500 for a spouse and US$4,000 per child per year, and F-1/J-1 holders must provide dependent health insurance.

accommodation_support.conditions: Room (double occupancy) covered as a billable AU expense. AU's ISSS undergraduate cost guide for 2026-2027 lists room at US$13,112.

board.conditions: Board (based on a 175-block meal plan) covered as a billable AU expense. AU's ISSS undergraduate cost guide for 2026-2027 lists board at US$6,584.

bond.note: No service bond or return-home requirement is published in the official sources. The award's preference criteria reference commitment to advancing the needs of under-resourced, underserved communities in the home country, but no contractual bond is published.

total_estimated_value.note: AU does not publish a total award value for the full AU EGLS. The only published award value is the AU EGL Partial Scholarship cap of up to US$40,000 per year.

partial_scholarship_award.conditions: Published as 'up to US$40,000/per year'. AU's First-Year Merit Awards page states up to eight additional AU EGL Partial Scholarships are offered. Recipients must submit proof of additional funds for the shortfall: for example, if offered US$40,000 per year the student must confirm US$42,000 on account for the first year instead of the full estimated costs of US$83,680.

coverage: Full tuition for all four years of undergraduate study (a billable AU expense)
On-campus room (double occupancy) for all four years
Board / meal plan for all four years
All billable AU expenses as defined by American University
Renewable for a total of four years of undergraduate study subject to continued satisfactory academic performance
coverage_limitations: Mandatory health insurance is NOT covered by the award.
Books are NOT covered by the award.
Airline tickets are NOT covered by the award.
Taxes are NOT covered by the award.
Miscellaneous and personal expenses are NOT covered by the award.
AU estimates these non-billable expenses at approximately US$4,000 per year, payable out of pocket.
US visa costs are not covered: the SEVIS fee, DS-160 form and the visa application fee are the student's responsibility, and AU publishes no amounts for them.
AU anticipates an increase of approximately 5-7% for each succeeding academic year, so the exact billable cost base the award covers will change annually.
AU EGL Partial Scholarships are capped at up to US$40,000 per year and require the recipient to document additional funds covering the shortfall.
The exact benefit structure may differ by academic year and by school within AU.
eligible_applicants: International students who will need a non-immigrant visa (preferably an F-1 or J-1 student visa) to study in the United States
First-year applicants to any bachelor's degree major offered at American University
Applicants who have not enrolled in or begun any post-secondary studies at another university in their home country or the United States
Applicants who graduated secondary school in 2024 or later (applicants who graduated secondary school earlier than 2024 are not eligible)
Preference is given to students who are still enrolled in secondary/high school and graduating by June 2027
final_year_condition: Final-year secondary/high school students are not only eligible but preferred: AU states that preference will be given to students who are still enrolled in secondary/high school and graduating by June 2027. Applicants who have already graduated from secondary school at the time of application must submit a short Interruption of Studies Statement describing their activities since graduation.
equivalent_degree_note: Equivalent secondary qualifications are accepted. AU asks applicants to include predicted or final examination results from exams such as IB, GCSE, GCE, Bagrut, French Baccalaureate, CAPE Units One and Two, Abitur, Attestat, or Secondary School Leaving Certificates. Students in 3-year secondary school systems submit transcripts for those three years. Native speakers of English from listed English-speaking countries who list English as their first language on the Common Application are not required to submit proof of English proficiency.

eligibility.citizenship: Not eligible: U.S. citizens, U.S. permanent residents, U.S. pending permanent residents, or dual citizens of the U.S. and another country. Open to nationals of all other countries.
eligibility.residence_requirement: Applicants must include a permanent address outside the United States, even if they currently live or study in the United States.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Applicants must be completing or have completed secondary school, graduating no earlier than 2024. Students still enrolled in secondary/high school and graduating by June 2027 are preferred.
eligibility.academic_requirements: No minimum GPA or fixed percentage is published. Selection is based on outstanding academic achievement combined with English communication skills, leadership, volunteerism and community service.
eligibility.language_requirement: Applicants must meet AU's English proficiency requirements, either by curriculum (four years of study in a U.S. institutionally accredited, IB, CXC or UK curriculum where English is the only medium of instruction and no ESL courses were taken, or four years in a listed English-speaking country/system under the same conditions) or by testing.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: Extracurricular achievement, volunteerism and community service feature strongly in the published preference criteria.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: A demonstrated commitment to leadership, volunteerism, community service, and to advancing the needs of people in the home country is an explicit preference criterion.
eligibility.financial_need: The AU EGLS is a merit scholarship, not a need-based award. No need-based financial aid is available to international students (non-U.S. citizens). Socioeconomic background enters only as a preference criterion: preference is given to students from diverse and underrepresented global and socioeconomic backgrounds. Undergraduate admission at AU is need-aware for all international students, meaning AU considers the student's ability to cover all costs when making admissions decisions.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: No restriction on holding a previous scholarship is published. Applicants not selected as finalists may still be considered for admission and for partial merit scholarships.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Applicants must not be enrolled in or have already begun any post-secondary studies at another university in their home country or the United States.
eligibility.field_restrictions: None. Students interested in all majors offered at AU are eligible to apply.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: AU publishes no minimum percentage, GPA or class rank for the AU EGLS.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Academic requirements are set by the individual school and major at AU; the AU EGLS is open to students in all majors offered at AU. AU publishes no major-specific AU EGLS thresholds.
selection_factors_may_include: Diverse and underrepresented global and socioeconomic backgrounds
Commitment to advancing the needs of people in the home country
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: AU describes its international merit awards as highly competitive and based on a combination of outstanding academic achievement, excellent communication skills in English, leadership, volunteerism, and community service. There is no published numeric score threshold.

english_requirement.moi_rule: English proficiency may be met via curriculum: four years of study (grades 9, 10, 11 and 12 or equivalent) in a U.S. institutionally accredited or IB, CXC, or UK curriculum (inside or outside the U.S.) where English is the only medium of instruction AND no ESL courses have been taken; or four years of study in the selected English-speaking countries (U.S., UK and Ireland, Scotland, Wales, Australia, New Zealand, Canada except Quebec, Singapore, Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Nigeria, South Africa, Zambia, Zimbabwe, and listed Caribbean countries) or in the educational systems of these countries under the same conditions.
english_requirement.test_score_note: AU publishes the following minimum test scores: TOEFL 85/4.5 (the source page does not define the second figure), IELTS 6.5, Cambridge English 176, Duolingo English Test 120, Pearson Test of English 60, LanguageCERT Academic 70, SAT-EBRW 610. Only official test scores are accepted and students cannot self-report exam results. Meeting the minimum score does not guarantee admission. For the AU EGLS specifically, official English proficiency score reports must be sent directly by the testing agency to American University before 15 January 2027. Native speakers of English from the listed countries who list English as their first language on the Common Application are not required to submit proof of English proficiency, though it may be requested. AU states the Office of Admissions may still request scores or additional documentation if deemed necessary.

language_of_instruction.language_note: All American University bachelor's degree programmes are taught in English. English proficiency must be demonstrated either by curriculum or by testing, and recommendation letters must be in English.

application_method.application_route: Two-step: Step 1 is the Common Application with all required supporting documents per AU's international instructions checklist; Step 2 is the AU EGLS application and essays submitted through the applicant's AU applicant portal (the Future Eagle Portal), which is created after the Common Application is submitted.
application_steps: Step 1 — Complete and submit the Common Application with all required documents per the AU international instructions checklist before 15 January 2027.
Create your applicant portal (Future Eagle Portal) when invited to do so.
Step 2 — Submit the AU EGLS application and essays via the applicant portal by 15 January 2027. Step 1 must be completed before Step 2. Late applications will not be considered.
Submit a bank letter and the completed and signed AU Declaration of Finances Form (AU DFF), each confirming a minimum of US$4,000, uploaded via the applicant portal.

Submit official TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo English Test, PTE, LanguageCERT or Cambridge Assessment English Test score results before 15 January 2027, sent directly by the testing agency to American University.
Complete Zoom interviews and/or additional essay submissions if selected as a semi-finalist or finalist.
application_method.application_fee: US$75 Common Application fee. Only first-year students applying for the AU EGLS and/or students referred directly by EducationUSA or other non-government organizations abroad may be eligible to receive an application fee waiver on a case-by-case basis; all other applicants must submit the US$75 fee.
application_method.multiple_applications_note: The application itself is online only. Transcripts and recommendation letters may alternatively be sent by courier to Undergraduate Admissions, Office of Enrollment, 4801 Massachusetts Ave., NW STE-218, Washington, DC 20016-8001, USA.
application_method.portal_note: AU does not publish a public direct URL for the AU EGLS application; it is accessed through the applicant portal created after the Common Application is submitted. AU's Decision Plans and Deadlines FAQ refers to this portal as the Future Eagle Portal.

selection_process.decision_maker: American University Office of Enrollment (Undergraduate Admissions / International Admissions) AU EGLS selection committee
selection_process.selection_type: Competitive multi-stage scholarship selection linked to, but separate from, the admission decision
possible_stages: Step 1: Common Application and all supporting documents submitted
Step 2: AU EGLS application and essays submitted via the applicant portal
Application review for admission and scholarship eligibility

selection_process.weighting_note: AU publishes no numeric weighting or scoring rubric for the AU EGLS. Selection rests on the published preference criteria and on outstanding academic achievement, excellent communication skills in English, leadership, volunteerism and community service.
selection_process.results_timing: Finalists and award winners will be notified by April 1, 2027 for the Fall 2027 entry cycle.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: AU's legacy Emerging Global Leader Scholarship page states that approximately 100 students apply each year against almost 1,000 inquiries, that five AU EGLS finalists are identified and must complete a rigorous series of Zoom interviews and special essays before a candidate is selected. That page still states the award is available for only one international student per year, which conflicts with the current pages stating two full awards.

selection_criteria.financial_need: Not a need-based award. No need-based financial aid is available to international students. Socioeconomic background is a stated preference factor (students from diverse and underrepresented socioeconomic backgrounds) but no financial-needs test is published. Note that undergraduate admission at AU is need-aware for all international students.
additional_factors: International students who have overcome various obstacles and challenges
Students from diverse and underrepresented global and socioeconomic backgrounds
Demonstrated commitment to leadership, volunteerism, community service, and to advancing the needs of people in the home country
Students who meet AU's English proficiency requirements
Students who are still enrolled in secondary/high school and graduating by June 2027

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: Bachelor's degree in any major offered at American University
possible_awards: AU Emerging Global Leader Scholarship — all billable AU expenses (full tuition, room, board)
AU EGL Partial Scholarship — up to US$40,000 per year
AU first-year partial merit scholarship — US$8,000 to US$25,000 per academic year (separate from the AU EGL Partial Scholarships)
degree_outcome.degree_note: Students interested in all majors offered at AU are eligible to apply for the AU EGLS. The award is tied to first-year entry; applicants who are not selected as finalists may still be considered for admission to American University and eligible for partial merit scholarships.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: AU accepts a maximum of 30 credit hours from one or a combination of specific examinations. Advanced credit may be available for IB, A Level, AP, OIB English or CAPE Unit Two exams passed during secondary school.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Full tuition is covered as a billable AU expense. AU charges tuition per semester, per credit hour; the published ISSS undergraduate cost guide for 2026-2027 lists US$62,680 at 12-17 credits per semester, plus US$1,700 in mandatory fees.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: US$75 Common Application fee applies. AU states that only first-year students applying for the AU EGLS and/or students referred directly by EducationUSA or other non-government organizations abroad may be eligible to receive an application fee waiver on a case-by-case basis.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: No separate scholarship agreement PDF is published. The AU Declaration of Finances Form (AU DFF) must be completed, signed and dated within the past three months, and no typed names are accepted on the later CFIS form.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: AU's Emerging Global Leader Scholarship page states that EGLS scholars serve as AU Diplomat international student ambassadors. This is described as an ambassadorial role, not a contractual service obligation.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: No bond or service obligation is published, so no breach consequence is published. Renewal depends on continued satisfactory academic performance.

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: The essays should be built around the published preference criteria rather than a generic personal statement: (1) obstacles and challenges overcome and a diverse or socioeconomic-underrepresented background; (2) demonstrated commitment to leadership, volunteerism and community service; (3) concrete plans to advance the needs of people in the home country and to improve under-resourced, underserved communities. AU also references AU EGLS scholars serving as AU Diplomat international student ambassadors, so a global-engagement and civic-change narrative fits the award's stated purpose.

common_mistakes: Assuming the scholarship is automatic on admission — a separate two-step EGLS application and essays are required

risk_flags.risk: Conflicting published deadlines: the AU EGLS application page states 15 January 2027, while the Decision Plans and Deadlines FAQ states applicants must submit the Common Application prior to December 1 and the AU EGL Scholarship application via the Future Eagle Portal by December 1.
risk_flags.impact: An applicant who follows the later date could miss the scholarship entirely even though the application page permits it.
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat 1 December 2026 as the working deadline and confirm directly with intadm@american.edu before relying on 15 January.

risk_flags.risk: Only two full AU EGLS awards are offered per entry cycle, against roughly 100 applicants annually per AU's own legacy page.
risk_flags.impact: Extremely low probability of receiving the full award.
risk_flags.mitigation: Apply equally for AU first-year partial merit scholarships (US$8,000-US$25,000 per year) and for external funding; note that non-finalists may still be admitted with partial merit scholarships.

risk_flags.risk: The award does not cover mandatory health insurance, books, airfare, taxes and miscellaneous expenses — approximately US$4,000 per year — nor any U.S. visa fees.
risk_flags.impact: Recipients still need personal funds and a valid financial document set, and AU anticipates 5-7% annual cost increases.
risk_flags.mitigation: Budget the non-billable costs plus SEVIS fee, DS-160 and visa fee, and plan for annual increases over four years.

risk_flags.risk: The number of full awards is inconsistent across AU's own live pages: the legacy au-egls.cfm page still says the scholarship is available for only one international student per year, while the current apply and merit pages say two.
risk_flags.impact: Recorded award counts and applicant odds may be stale or wrong.
risk_flags.mitigation: Verify the current award count with International Admissions before publication and update this record each cycle.

risk_flags.risk: Partial scholarship recipients must document additional funds beyond the initial US$4,000 to cover the shortfall — for example US$42,000 on account for a US$40,000 per year award.
risk_flags.impact: A partial offer is conditional on proving funds the applicant may not have.
risk_flags.mitigation: Assess fund availability before relying on a partial award; AU's full first-year cost estimate is published as US$87,374 on the international instructions checklist (US$83,680 on the First-Year Merit Awards page).

risk_flags.risk: Undergraduate admission at AU is need-aware for all international students, so ability to cover all costs affects the admission decision itself.
risk_flags.impact: Financial documentation quality can affect admission, not just scholarship consideration.
risk_flags.mitigation: Submit a clean, recent, letterhead bank letter and a correctly signed AU DFF by the deadline.

risk_flags.risk: Strict eligibility cut-offs: applicants who have begun post-secondary study, or who graduated secondary school before 2024, or who hold U.S. citizenship, permanent residency, pending permanent residency or dual U.S. citizenship are excluded.
risk_flags.mitigation: Confirm status before investing in test scores and the application.

risk_flags.risk: U.S. visa exposure: effective 6 September 2025 the U.S. Department of State requires nonimmigrant visa applicants to apply in their country of nationality or residence, and AU notes temporary freezes in scheduling certain F and J visa interviews.
risk_flags.impact: Even a funded, admitted student may be unable to enter the United States on schedule.
risk_flags.mitigation: Check current U.S. Department of State guidance and interview availability in the applicant's country of nationality or residence well before the semester start.

database_notes: Cycle researched: Fall 2027 entry. AU's dedicated AU EGLS application page publishes 15 January 2027 for both application steps and 1 April 2027 for notification, so this record is current as of 2026-10-10.

Official award name is 'AU Emerging Global Leader Scholarship (AU EGLS)'. AU also uses 'AU Emerging Global Leadership Scholarship', 'AU EGL Scholarship' and 'AU EGLs' on its own pages; these are recorded in legacy_titles.

The full award is described by AU as covering 'all billable AU expenses (full tuition, room, and board)' for two international students. It is NOT an all-inclusive full ride: mandatory health insurance, books, airline tickets, taxes and miscellaneous expenses are excluded at approximately US$4,000 per year. fully_funded is therefore set to false with an explanatory note.

The approximately US$4,000 per year figure for non-billable expenses is AU's own published estimate on the AU EGLS pages. AU's ISSS AY 2026-2027 undergraduate cost guide itemizes books at US$1,200, health insurance at US$2,506 and personal expenses at US$2,044, which sums to more than US$4,000; both figures are recorded rather than reconciled, because AU does not reconcile them.

Deadline conflict recorded as a risk flag: the AU EGLS application page states 15 January 2027, while the Decision Plans and Deadlines FAQ states that EGLS applicants must submit the Common Application prior to December 1 and the AU EGL Scholarship application via the Future Eagle Portal by December 1. The award-specific page was treated as authoritative for deadline_date, but the earlier date should be used for planning.

Award-count conflict recorded: the legacy au-egls.cfm page still states the scholarship is available for only one international student per year, whereas the current AU EGLS application page and First-Year Merit Awards page both state two. The current figure of two was used.

Partial-scholarship count: 'up to eight' AU EGL Partial Scholarships appears only on the First-Year Merit Awards page, not on the dedicated AU EGLS application page. This is recorded but flagged as unverified.

AU's published TOEFL minimum is rendered '85/4.5'. The source does not define the second figure, so minimum_toefl is recorded as 85 with the full published string preserved in test_score_note rather than interpreting 4.5.
bachelor_requirement is set to false because the AU EGLS is an award to study FOR a bachelor's degree; it requires completed or impending secondary school, not a prior bachelor's degree.

Equivalent secondary qualifications are accepted and AU describes 3-year secondary school systems, IB/GCSE/GCE/Bagrut/French Baccalaureate/CAPE/Abitur/Attestat examinations and English-medium curriculum routes, so equivalent_degree_allowed is true.
previous_emjm_scholarship_ineligible is false because this is not an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's award and the concept does not apply; no previous-award restriction on re-application is published.

official_programme_guide_url is null: no AU EGLS rulebook, handbook or policy PDF exists. The AU Declaration of Finances Form and Instructions PDF is an application form, not a programme guide, and is referenced in document_checklist.financial_documents instead.

official_catalogue_url is set to AU's First-Year Merit Awards page, which is AU's catalogue page listing the AU EGLS alongside its other international first-year merit awards. The deeper award-specific page is recorded in official_source_url.

portal_url is null because AU does not publish a public direct URL for the AU EGLS application; it is accessed through the applicant portal created after the Common Application is submitted. AU's Decision Plans and Deadlines FAQ names this the Future Eagle Portal.

financial_need is recorded as not a need-based award, but admission at AU is need-aware for all international students: AU states that it considers the student's ability to cover all costs when making admissions decisions. No need-based financial aid is available to international students (non-U.S. citizens).

The applicant pool figure of approximately 100 applicants per year against almost 1,000 inquiries, and the five-finalist structure, come from AU's legacy au-egls.cfm page, which also carries older figures for award count. These are presented as AU-published historical/context figures rather than current-cycle guarantees.
The 'AU Diplomat international student ambassador' role is described on AU's legacy EGLS page as what EGLS scholars do; it is not a contractual bond or service obligation, and no bond is published.

Visa-cost detail (SEVIS fee, DS-160, visa application fee) is recorded as not published: AU's Applying for a Visa page lists these as required steps without amounts, and no non-official source was used to fill the gap.

The logo is the official American University crest-and-wordmark asset hosted on the american.edu domain and referenced from the schema.org structured data of AU's own official pages. It was verified with a live HTTP HEAD request returning 200, Content-Type image/png and Content-Length 38,037 bytes. No third-party aggregator, blog or stock source was used. No verified photograph was sourced, so image_url is null.
All monetary figures in this record are transcribed from official american.edu pages and are denominated in USD. No total four-year award value has been computed or presented as an award.
